title: Zenith Payments - POC scoping: timeline & milestones
summary: POC scoping focused on timeline, milestones, success criteria and benchmarking plan for Zenlth Payments. Primary workstreams: infra access & network, sample dataset and workload sizing, performance benchmarks (latency, throughput, p50/p95), cost projection, and exec readout. Agreed 6-week pilot with kickoff next week, mid-point review at week 3, and executive readout at week 6. Action items assigned for SOW, environment access, and benchmark scripts.
milestones: Week 0: Kickoff & requirements alignment; Week 1: Access setup (VPN, service account, S3 samples, test keys) and baseline smoke tests; Week 2: Run initial benchmarks on 10k sample requests; Week 3: Mid-point review (performance & quality checkpoints, tuning); Week 4-5: Iterative optimization, dedicated config trials (batching, quantization, routing); Week 6: Exec readout with runbook, pass/fail criteria, and recommendation for next phase (dedicated vs hosted).
next_steps: Emma Li - share draft SOW and pricing by 2025-08-15
Zenith - provide sample dataset access (anonymized) and test accounts by 2025-08-14
Carlos - send benchmark script and runbook link
action_items: Emma Li: Draft SOW and send to Maya (due 2025-08-15)
Maya Patel: Share anonymized sample dataset link and list of top 10 query types (due 2025-08-14)
Samir Desai: Whitelist Redwood IPs and create service account (due 2025-08-16)
Carlos Mendes: Provide benchmark scripts, instructions and expected metrics (due 2025-08-13)
Priya Nair: Prepare success criteria doc for exec readout (due 2025-08-20)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-12 15:00 PT | Duration: ~45 minutes | Attendees: Emma Li (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Zenith Head of Eng), Evan Ross (Zenith SRE), Priya Nair (Product), Samir Desai (Infra), Janelle Kim (Security)

Summary: Quick alignment on POC scope, detailed timeline, and milestones. Focus on workload sizing, benchmark plan, network/KMS requirements, and success criteria. Agreed on a 6-week pilot.

[00:00] Emma (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Emma, AE at Redwood, and Carlos is our solutions engineer. Can we do a quick round of intros from the Zenith side?
[00:12] Maya (Zenith): Sure, Maya here, head of engineering. Evan SRE, Priya product, Samir infra, Janelle security. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:20] Emma: Awesome. The goal today is to scope the POC timeline and agree on milestones — kickoff, access setup, midpoint review, and exec readout. Also want to capture success criteria — performance, cost, and quality.
[00:35] Carlos (SE): Hi all. I'll walk through the benchmark plan and what we need for access. High level: we'll run generation and embedding workloads, measure p50/p95 latency, throughput (QPS), and cost per 1M tokens for your traffic mix.
[00:50] Evan: For context, our typical volume is around 120k requests/day for fraud scoring pipelines, peak concurrency about 80 concurrent requests in bursts, and embedding batch jobs run overnight — roughly 2M records weekly for batch.
[01:10] Carlos: Great, that's helpful. For the POC we usually do a representative sample — for real-time gen tests we'll use a 10k request sample with the burst profile, and for embeddings a 50k subset to validate batching and throughput.
[01:28] Priya: Our success criteria from product: p50 under 200ms for simple lookups, p95 under 800ms for complex generation, and embeddings throughput that can finish nightly jobs in our maintenance window. Also need cost estimates — we have a target to at least cut current per-request cost by 25%.
[01:50] Emma: Noted. We'll include cost-per-inference comparisons and advise on dedicated vs hosted. For sensitive data, Samir and Janelle, can you outline any network or compliance constraints?
[02:05] Janelle (Security): SOC2 is a must, we require audit logs, KMS-managed keys, and SSO with SAML integration. For POC, we can allow a locked-down staging VPC peering or allow Redwood to egress via whitelisted IPs. No customer PII in raw logs — anonymized dataset only.
[02:30] Samir (Infra): We prefer VPC peering if possible, but can do IP whitelisting to start. We'll need a service account and an S3 bucket with the sample dataset. Also want to understand latency impact if we go to a hosted region vs deploying private.
[02:50] Carlos: OK, for the POC hosted path we'll route to our closest region; we'll capture network latency in the benchmarks. If needed, we can test a private deployment later to show delta.
[03:05] Emma: Timeline proposal: Kickoff next week (target 2025-08-19), 6-week POC: week 1 access & smoke tests, week 2 initial benchmarks, week 3 mid-point review to evaluate tuning, weeks 4-5 optimization and dedicated config trials, week 6 exec readout. Thoughts?
[03:25] Maya: That aligns with our internal calendar. Execs want results in about six weeks — good. 
[03:32] Evan: For benchmarking, we need the exact scripts. Do you provide them?
[03:37] Carlos: Yes — we'll share a benchmark repo with scripts for generation and embedding, instructions to stage data, and an automated runner. Expect p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost estimates in the report.
[03:50] Priya: For quality success criteria, we'll also want a small eval set and human-review pass rates — e.g., less than 5% regression vs baseline for critical prompts.
[04:05] Emma: We'll include a small eval harness and suggested prompts. We'll also run automatic comparisons and flag any quality regressions.
[04:18] Maya: Important to capture edge cases — our fraud prompts are terse and often have token limits. Any constraints on sequence length?
[04:27] Carlos: We'll run at your typical sequence lengths. Our runtime supports KV cache and smart batching; we'll note memory impact. If you need long context, we'll recommend specific model/quantization profiles.
[04:40] Samir: On encryption, we must use our KMS keys for any stored artifacts. Is that supported?
[04:45] Emma: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for hosted POC we can arrange encrypted storage and limited KMS integration — we'll include options in the SOW.
[04:58] Janelle: Audit logs — we need request-level logs for the POC. What retention do you recommend?
[05:05] Carlos: For POC, short retention (30 days) is typical; we can increase retention for compliance at extra cost. We'll make sure logs are accessible via console or exported to your S3.
[05:18] Maya: Ok, that covers security. Let's talk success criteria concretely so we can present to execs: performance (p50/p95 targets), cost (<= 25% improvement), stability (error rate <0.1%), and quality (<=5% regression).
[05:36] Emma: That's a good set. We'll formalize those in a success criteria doc for the exec readout.
[05:42] Carlos: Benchmarks: we'll run three profiles — 1) Real-time generation (bursty QPS), 2) Embeddings batch (throughput and batching efficiency), 3) Mixed small request workloads. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, throughput, CPU/GPU utilization.
[06:05] Evan: For batch embeddings we need to ensure completion within our 4-hour window. For generation, p95 under 800ms is okay for now.
[06:15] Carlos: We'll include a run that simulates your nightly batch and another that stresses peak concurrency.
[06:22] Priya: Any chance we can test quantized models? We've seen cost benefits elsewhere.
[06:27] Emma: Yes, we can test INT8/4 quantized variants as part of the optimization phase. We'll surface quality tradeoffs.
[06:35] Maya: Are there any additional infra tasks on our side?
[06:38] Samir: We'll need to create the service account, whitelist IPs (or arrange peering), and provide S3 read access to a sample bucket. We'll also point to any internal proxies.
[06:48] Emma: Great — Carlos will send a checklist.
[06:51] Carlos: I'll send the benchmark repo link and a checklist with exact network/keys instructions. We'll also include Terraform snippets for service accounts.
[07:00] Emma: Logistics: kickoff 2025-08-19. Deliverables from Redwood: SOW + pricing, benchmark scripts, runbook, and initial smoke test report. From Zenith: dataset access, service account, and whitelist.
[07:15] Priya: For exec readout, we need an executive summary + two options: go hosted with optimizations or move to Dedicated capacity. Please include cost delta and estimated timeline to prod.
[07:27] Emma: We'll prepare a decision matrix for the readout.
[07:32] Maya: On the SOW, can you include an optional dedicated trial so we can see performance delta?
[07:38] Emma: Yes, we'll include an optional one-week dedicated trial in the SOW pricing as an add-on.
[07:44] Janelle: Quick security Q: will logs include the raw query? We said no PII in logs.
[07:50] Carlos: We can redact or hash sensitive fields in logs and store a mapping in your environment only. We'll document that approach.
[07:58] Evan: For the benchmark script, can it run from our infra to measure end-to-end latency?
[08:03] Carlos: Absolutely — the runner can be executed from your VMs; it'll report end-to-end latency and show breakdowns.
[08:11] Emma: Ok let's capture next steps and owners. We've put those in the action items. Anything else?
[08:19] Priya: One last ask — include a sample delivery of the final runbook and a template for the exec slide deck.
[08:24] Emma: We'll provide that.
[08:27] Maya: Thanks, this is helpful. Looking forward to the kickoff.

[08:35] (wrap-up noise, quick confirmations)

NOTES/REFERENCES: Benchmark repo (short link): https://redwood.ai/bench/zenith-poc (placeholder) — contains scripts, Terraform snippets, and runbook. Draft SOW link: https://redwood.ai/sow/drafts/zenith (placeholder).

End of transcript.
